# dsh-visualrules
Workspace profiles, team rules, commit validation, and session-scoped rule injection for DeepSeek Ha
pace profiles, team rules, commit validation, and session-scoped rule injection for DeepSeek Harness
See the rules. Enforce the commit. Teach the model. Leave the repository untouched.
🌏 中文 · English
## Why this plugin
A DSH session can move between repositories, teams, and environments in a single afternoon. Each pla
ce has its own Git identity, branch convention, protected branches, commit format, and review policy
. Most of that knowledge lives in `CONTRIBUTING.md`, a commitlint config, a group chat, or somebody'
s memory — invisible to the model and easy to violate at 2 a.m.
**dsh-visualrules** turns those rules into a first-class workspace surface:
- **Visible** — the session header shows the environment; one click opens identity, branch, remote,

environment, and rule summary in the native right sidebar.
- **Enforced** — AI-issued `git commit` /
branch creation passes a rule engine before it runs, and an optional pair of Git hooks covers the t

erminal, IDE, scripts, and background tasks.
- **Injected** — enabled rule packs are appended to the
session's system prompt, scoped to the session directory, budgeted against the model context window

, and previewable before you enable them.
- **Traceable** — every block, warning, one-time bypass, a
nd AI-authored commit hash is indexed locally.
The plugin never edits `agents.md`, never writes the repository, never changes Git config, and never
stores a password, token, or private-key content.

with colour semantics, branch / remote / upstream / ahead-behind, protected-branch and naming warni

| **📚 Rule packs**
Create, import Markdown, edit, enable globally or per workspace, and r
euse one pack across repositories. Team packs can live in the repository (`file:`) or inline (`conte

nt:`), and stay read-only in the plugin.
F0.1, F0.4, F0.6 | **💉 Session injection**
Personal → team
→ workspace supplement, with the later layer winning. A live preview shows the exact text, character

count, budget, and truncation before the next model step receives it.
F0.2, F0.3, F0.5 |
| **🛡️ Com

mit validation**
Identity, protected branch, branch naming, Conventional Commits, allowed types, sco
pe, header length, linked Issue, merge-message mismatch, and `--no-verify` visibility. Every rule is

`off / info / warn / block` per workspace.
F2.1–F2.4, F2.6 | **🤖 Model-facing rejection**
A blocked
tool call returns the violated rule, its source, and a concrete fix. The model reads it in the next
step and can retry correctly — no opaque “command failed”. `visualrules_check` lets it pre-flight a

message or branch.
F2.8 |
| **🪝 Optional Git hooks**
Two managed hooks (`pre-commit`, `commit-msg`)
cover human commits. An existing hook is backed up and still runs first; uninstall restores it. A `

core.hooksPath` outside the repository is refused.
F2.9 | **🔓 User-only bypass**
A blocked commit ca
n be released for exactly one commit with a written reason and a 5–30 minute TTL. The agent cannot c

reate a bypass; only the UI can.
F2.7 |
| **🧭 AI commit index**

### 3. Enable a rule pack
Open **Workspace → Rule packs → New**, or use **Create the default pack** from an empty state. Tick
a pack on for the current workspace. The right-sidebar preview and the Injection preview update imme
diately; the next request uses the new text. Changes apply on the **next model request**, never retr

## Compatibility

- DSH **0.2.2-rc.1+** (verified on the desktop profile).
- Node.js **20+** for the standalone hook r

unner (`node` must be on `PATH` for Git hooks).
- macOS, Linux, and Windows Git Bash are supported b

y the hook scripts; the UI follows the host theme.
- No native dependencies; the only runtime depend
encies are `yaml` and `zod`.
